shortDescription: A tram-linked Polish city where rented housing, public schools, workshops, libraries and the visible legacy of textile industry overlap with post-2004 redevelopment and European mobility.
longDescription: This World is rooted in Łódź, Poland, an inland city whose residential districts, tram lines, rail stations, workshops and former textile-industrial buildings remain visibly intertwined. Two caregivers and two siblings share a rented home while work schedules, transit, energy costs and repair of durable goods shape routine planning. Public school, municipal libraries, practical workshops, cultural programs and rail connections create varied contact beyond the household. Across 2004–2026, EU-era mobility, redevelopment, changing retail and digital life alter the city's surface without erasing its tram network and post-industrial urban fabric.

visualProfile.overallCharacter: Working Central European city life where ordinary homes, tram infrastructure, workshops, converted industrial buildings and civic institutions coexist without industrial-grit caricature.
visualProfile.geographyAndClimate: Inland Polish climate with visible seasons: cold gray or snowy winters, wet transitional months and warmer green summers; no single season should define the World.
visualProfile.builtEnvironment: Older low-rise and rented residential buildings, brick or masonry industrial remnants, workshops and small businesses, Polish public-school buildings, MPK-Łódź tram infrastructure, rail approaches, libraries and cultural spaces.
visualProfile.streetsAndPublicRealm: Tram tracks and overhead wires, stops used by students and shift workers, mixed residential-commercial streets, repair shops, bakeries, second-hand retail, rail-station approaches and redeveloped former-industrial areas.
visualProfile.interiors: Budget-conscious rented-home interiors, school classrooms and practical/technical spaces, workbenches and repair shops, municipal-library reading/computer areas and modest exhibition or meeting rooms.
visualProfile.materialsAndTextures: Brick, plaster, concrete, steel rails, tram wire, worn paving, painted wood or laminate interiors, workshop metal, tools, paper schedules, books and repaired household appliances.
visualProfile.lightAndAtmosphere: Soft overcast Central European light, low winter sun, warm interior lighting in workshops and homes, clearer summer daylight and ordinary municipal street lighting rather than cinematic industrial darkness.
visualProfile.vegetationAndLandscape: Street trees, courtyards, small planted areas and seasonal greenery sit within dense urban fabric; avoid replacing the city with either industrial wasteland or suburban parkland.
visualProfile.mobilityAndVehicles: Walking, MPK trams and buses are routine; regional/intercity rail is visible for occasional movement. Bicycles and practical cars/service vehicles may appear, but household identity should not be car-centered.
visualProfile.signageAndLanguage: Polish dominates civic, school, transit and shop signage. English is common in school, media and later commercial/digital contexts; German may appear in language study, travel or historical/business contexts but should not dominate the streetscape.
visualProfile.clothingAndEverydayObjects: Contemporary Polish urban clothing appropriate to season; school backpacks, transit passes/tickets, work jackets, tools, bakery or grocery bags, second-hand household goods, phones, notebooks and repaired appliances.
visualProfile.technologyAndInfrastructure: Period-correct trams, buses, school computers, household electronics and phones should evolve across 2004–2026; converted industrial spaces and modernized transit/commercial surfaces can become more visible over time without making every district newly renovated.
visualProfile.publicInstitutions: Polish public school, MPK-Łódź trams/buses, regional rail, municipal libraries, cultural programs and practical/vocational workshops should remain recognizable parts of ordinary life.

temporalLayers.2004_2010: Early post-EU-accession period with older mobile phones, more paper transit information, less renovated industrial property and fewer digitally mediated services; trams, rail and repair commerce remain central.
temporalLayers.2011_2018: Smartphones and digital media become ordinary, redevelopment and adaptive reuse become more visible, and English-language commercial cues increase while older residential/workshop streets persist.
temporalLayers.2019_2026: More modernized transit information, newer phones and digital services, additional renovated former-industrial spaces and contemporary retail can appear beside long-standing tram corridors and budget-conscious housing.
temporalLayers.continuities: Polish-language public life, tram-based mobility, rail connections, older industrial fabric, repair/second-hand commerce, public schools and municipal cultural institutions remain stable visual anchors.

avoid: luxury redevelopment presented as the whole city
moralized contrast between academic and practical work
